summary: The candidate's capture guard is a verified crash-avoidance correction for unsupported ragged-verify backends and is preserved. Independent inspection confirms that Triton-backed hybrid target verification is deliberately routed to eager execution. The original B300/CUDA 13.2 extend_attention_fwd illegal memory access and compact CUDA-graph execution could not be reproduced or safely corrected on the available AMD ROCm host without the Qwen hybrid and DSpark weights.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before: unsupported compact capture entered warmup; 5 tests passed and the issue-specific test errored. Raw output: reports/j-04c3392fd38a/evidence/failing-before.log

Passing-after: 6 tests passed, covering Triton/hybrid capability composition, unsupported capture skip plus eager replay admission, supported compact continuation, and non-compact continuation. Raw output: reports/j-04c3392fd38a/evidence/passing-after.log

gpu_execution.evidence: The focused tests imported GPU backend modules but did not execute extend_attention_fwd or a numerical GPU workload. Environment evidence identifies the only device as AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950 with ROCm 7.2 and no CUDA runtime: reports/j-04c3392fd38a/evidence/environment.log

remaining_limitations: The report requires NVIDIA B300/CUDA 13.2; the assigned device is AMD MI350X/gfx950 under ROCm 7.2.
Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6 hybrid and DSpark model weights were unavailable.
The exact batch-size-20, eight-tokens-per-request illegal memory access was not reproduced.
The regression proves capture and replay admission control with mocks; it does not execute extend_attention_fwd or a full-attention/GatedDeltaNet model.
Compact target-verify CUDA-graph execution remains unsupported for Triton-backed hybrid attention and falls back to eager execution.
